a: A unit test checks a small piece of code (function/class) in isolation.
An integration test checks that multiple parts work together (e.g. API + database).
End-to-end tests simulate real user flows through the whole system.
TDD means write a failing test first, then code until it passes, then refactor.
A mock replaces a dependency with a controlled fake for testing.
A stub returns canned responses so tests do not call real services.
Test coverage measures how much of the code is executed by tests.
A regression is a bug that reappears after something that used to work breaks.
A smoke test is a quick check that the main paths still work after a deploy.
Load testing measures how a system behaves under expected or high traffic.
Stress testing pushes a system beyond normal limits to find breaking points.
A flaky test sometimes passes and sometimes fails without code changes.
An assertion checks that a condition is true in a test; failure fails the test.
QA (Quality Assurance) processes aim to prevent and catch defects before users do.
